and benefits for retirement, disability, and death; and to levy a special tax
therefor not exceeding 1/2 of one mill. To enter into contracts, and do any and
all other things necessary in order to completely co-operate with fire
districts organized under the laws of Idaho; to purchase and maintain fire
fighting equipment and employ firemen in connection therewith; to authorize the
sending of fire fighting equipment and firemen employed by the city of Boise to
any point in said districts; to appropriate money therefor. To regulate the
installation of electric wiring, fixtures and apparatus; to regulate the
storage of photographic films, and the manner and places motion picture films
may be used or exhibited; and to regulate the erection of chimneys, flues and
fireplaces, and to provide regulations for securing their competent
construction. To provide by ordinance civil service or merit systems covering
all, or any part of, the officers and employees of the city who are not elected
or are not the head of a department.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939. Ch. 41 S.L. 1949.
OBSTRUCTION OF STREETS-HIGHWAYS, ETC.
SECTION 42(16). To provide for the prevention and removal of encroachments and
obstructions from the streets, sidewalks, alleys, or other highways and public
places of the city, and for the cleaning and repairing of the same, and to
compel owners, lessees, agents, and occupants of lands abutting thereon to
remove such obstructions and repair such streets, sidewalks, alleys, or other
highways and public places of the city and to punish such persons for refusing
so to do.
   ANNOTATIONS:
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
   Wilson v. Boise City, 6 Ida. 397, 55 Pac. 889.
MARKET AND SLAUGHTER HOUSES FOOD-FUEL
SECTION 42(17). To provide for the establishment of market houses and places,
and to regulate the location and management of market houses, hide houses and
places; to prohibit and regulate the location and management of slaughter
houses, hide houses, and other offensive places or factories within five miles
of the city limits; and to provide a standard of weights and measures, and of
food and fuel, and to prevent and prohibit the sale of unhealthful and
unwholesome food; to regulate the disposition and destruction of foods; and to
provide for the office of city weigher and measurer.
   ANNOTATIONS:
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
   In re Snyder, 10 Ida. 696, 79 Pac. 824.
PUBLIC BUILDINGS
SECTION 42(18). To purchase sites for and provide for the erection and
maintenance of city jails, houses of correction, work houses and any other
buildings for municipal or public purposes and for the government and
management of the same, both within and without the city limits.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
EXPLOSIVES
SECTION 42(19). To regulate, prohibit, and license the storage, or disposition
or manufacture, or transportation or use of anything whatsoever which is
explosive, combustible, poisonous, or dangerous, and to prevent by all possible
and proper means danger or risks of injury or damage by fire arising from
carelessness, negligence or otherwise.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
DISTURBANCE OF PEACE
SECTION 42(20). To restrain and punish intoxication, fighting and quarreling or
any disturbance or any unlawful or indecent practice, and to define what shall
constitute the same.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
FIREARMS
SECTION 42(21). To regulate, prohibit and license the sale, disposal, storage
or use of guns, pistols and firearms, fireworks, bombs and detonating works of
all descriptions.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
RIOTS
SECTION 42(22). To prevent, restrain, punish and disperse any riot or riotous
assemblage, or punish any person taking part therein.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
DANGEROUS WEAPONS
SECTION 42(23). To prohibit the carrying of dangerous weapons in a concealed
manner.
   ANNOTATIONS:
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
   State v. Hart, 66 Ida. 217, 157 P.(2) 72.
OFFENSIVE OCCUPATION
SECTION 42(24). To license, tax, control and regulate businesses, trades, and
occupations offensive to the senses or noxious to the health and to provide for
their exclusion from the city limits or any part thereof.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
CRUELTY TO ANIMALS
SECTION 42(25). To regulate the driving of animals through the streets and
prevent cruelty to animals and children.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
IMPOUNDING ANIMALS
SECTION 42(26). To prevent any and all animals from running at large within the
city limits, or any part thereof, and to punish those persons who allow animals
to so run at large; and to provide for their impounding, and also for the sale,
of such animals upon five days' notice; and to authorize the destruction of
animals when at large, contrary to any prohibition of any such ordinance; to
impose license taxes on dogs, cats, and other animals.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
SEWER CONNECTIONS
SECTION 42(27). To compel all persons erecting or maintaining privies, septic
tanks, waste outlets, cesspools or toilets within one hundred seventy feet of
any sewer to connect the same therewith; and to levy special taxes or to charge
and collect service charges for the privilege of connecting with sewers and for
the continued use thereof, the proceeds thereof to be used in construction,
operation, extension, replacement, enlargement, maintenance and repair of
sewers and sewage disposal facilities; to levy special taxes or to charge
service charges for the collection and disposal of trash or garbage.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939. Ch. 226 S.L. 1947.
PURCHASE OF PROPERTY AT TAX SALE
SECTION 42(28). To purchase, take and hold real property against which there is
a delinquent tax or assessment levied or imposed under the authority of Boise
City when sold for taxes, and to sell the same.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
SURVEYS
SECTION 42(29). To provide for the surveying of the blocks and streets of the
city, and for making the boundary lines of such blocks and streets.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
REGULATION OF USE OF HIGHWAYS
SECTION 42(30). To regulate the use of streets, sidewalks, alleys or other
highways and public places; to regulate the transportation of combustibles,
explosives or dangerous things through the streets of the city; to prescribe
the width of tires on all vehicles, and the weight to be carried thereby; to
provide for the preservation of the streets, sidewalks, alleys and other
highways.
   ANNOTATIONS:
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
   Fosters, Inc. v. Boise City, 63 Ida. 201, 118 P.(2) 721.
SIDEWALKS-STREET PARKINGS-FENCES
SECTION 42(31). To regulate the use of sidewalks and street parkings and
prevent the extension of structures within the street line, and may prohibit or
regulate the building and use of fences.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
ELECTRIC WIRES-GAS AND SEWER PIPES
SECTION 42(32). To regulate the opening of street surfaces, the laying,
construction, maintenance and removal of underground wires, pipes and other
conduits, the building, excavation, and repairing of sewers, and the erection,
construction, maintenance or removal of electric, gas and other wires, pipes,
and structures and fixtures.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
IMPROVEMENT OF STREETS, ALLEYS AND SIDEWALKS
SECTION 42(33). To open and establish streets, alleys, sidewalks or other
highways and widen the same, and for that purpose to condemn property for the
city use, under such regulations as are provided by the general laws of Idaho.
To vacate streets, alleys, or other highways; to maintain, improve, light,
repair or beautify the highways, streets, alleys, and sidewalks of the city,
and to provide for the payment of the expense of any of the above either out of
the general levy, or by a special tax levy, or by levying special assessments
in the manner herein provided upon property which is specially benefited by any
of the foregoing, or by a combination of any thereof. Provided, however, no
special assessment shall be levied against property specially benefited for the
resurfacing of any street or alley without the consent of the property owners
of three-fourths of the front feet of the lots abutting on such proposed
improvement. Provided, however, that where any street within the corporate
boundaries has been designated as a part of a state highway the state of Idaho
shall pay the cost of any widening, construction, improvement, repair or
maintenance thereof required by its or by any of its departments having
jurisdiction of state highways, and pay any other cost or expense in connection
therewith authorized by law.
   ANNOTATIONS:
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
   Adleman v. Pierce, 6 Ida. 294, 55 Pac. 658.
   Ch. 226 S.L. 1947.
SPRINKLING-OILING
SECTION 42(34). To provide for the sprinkling, cleaning and oiling of all the
streets in said city, and, to provide for the payment of the expense thereof,
to levy a tax or special assessment upon the real property to be benefited
thereby, which shall be a lien upon said property until paid.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
SEWER DISTRICTS
SECTION 42(35). To construct, or cause to be constructed, or otherwise acquire
or secure the use of, sewers, or sewage, or trash, or garbage collection or
disposal facilities, or any one or more thereof alone or in combination; to
locate the same wholly or in part within or without the city; to organize
special improvement districts therefor covering the whole or parts of the city;
to include within such districts lands outside of and within five miles of the
city boundaries which may be served or benefited thereby and where in the
opinion of the common council, the protection of the health of the city
requires; to provide for the payment of the expense thereof by levy of special
assessments upon the properties within such districts which are specially
benefited thereby, or by special tax levy; or by the issuance of general
obligation bonds as hereinafter provided, or by a combination thereof; to
produce and sell by-products of or by such facilities; to maintain, operate,
enlarge, extend, and repair such facilities, and therefor to levy and collect
special taxes upon properties within the city and to charge and collect
periodic service charges against properties outside the city served thereby; to
fix, charge and collect reasonable periodic service charges for the service
rendered by such facilities, whether heretofore or hereafter constructed,
against owners or occupants of property served or capable of being served
thereby, or against such property; to provide methods for collection, and
penalties, including denial of service, for nonpayment of such charges, and for
reinstatement charges, and including certification of delinquent payments to
the tax collector and when so certified the same shall be a lien against the
property, and collectible as other taxes; to cooperate or contract with other
districts, municipalities, organizations or persons for the construction, use,
maintenance, operation or repair of such facilities of or by such districts,
municipalities, organizations or persons; to license or permit the connection
of such facilities by, or the use of service to, properties not within the
limits of a district or the city provided there be paid on behalf of such
property a fair amount in relation to original construction costs of such
facility, and a periodic service charge for maintenance, repair and operation
of such facilities or service.
   ANNOTATIONS:
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
   Boise City National Bank v. Boise City, 15 Ida. 793, 100 Pac. 93.
   Mix v. Board of County Commissioners (Lewiston), 18 Ida. 704, 112 Pac. 218.
   Boise Development Co., Ltd., v. Boise City, 30 Ida. 686, 167 Pac. 1034.
   Ch. 226 S.L. 1947.
PARKS
SECTION 42(36). To acquire by condemnation or otherwise, establish, operate,
regulate, maintain and improve crematories, cemeteries, mausoleums, or other
burial places, parks, public grounds and places, either within or without the
city limits; to levy and collect special taxes therefor; to fix charges for
crematory services, burial space and services, and perpetual care; to create,
maintain, administer and invest perpetual care funds and use income therefrom
for maintenance, care, operation and upkeep of burial facilities.
   ANNOTATIONS:
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
   Boise Development Co., Ltd., v. Boise City, 30 Ida. 686, 167 Pac. 1034.
   Stephenson v. Pioneer Irr. Dist., 49 Ida. 195, 288 Pac. 423.
   Ch. 226 S.L. 1947.
REGULATIONS OF USE OF STREETS, ETC.
SECTION 42(37). To regulate and prevent public orders and advertising notices,
the making of noises, music, or speeches in the streets, or public places, to
control, regulate and limit traffic on the streets, alleys, sidewalks, and
other highways and public places, to regulate, control and prohibit the use of
the streets, highways, public places and sidewalks and space below or above or
adjacent or contiguous to the same, including the use of signs, displays,
advertising, posts, poles, and other obstructions; to regulate and prohibit the
exhibition and hanging of placards and flags in or across the street, or from
houses or other buildings; to prohibit the exhibition of deformed or crippled
persons; and to prohibit all persons from begging upon the streets or any other
public places; to establish from time to time such public stations as may be
necessary; to regulate the numbering of houses and lots on the street and
highways, and the naming of streets and highways; to prohibit persons from
roaming the streets at unreasonable hours.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
BUILDINGS
SECTION 42(38). To regulate or prevent the erection or moving of buildings
within the city limits, and in case any building shall become dangerous to
persons or property, or a fire or other hazard, to cause the same to be removed
or abated, or made safe, at the expense of the property, unless the owner shall
promptly do so upon five days' notice of such condition served personally or by
mail upon the owner thereof or his agent or representative, general or special,
respecting said property; to collect such expense, including making the same a
lien upon the property and foreclosing such lien, or by certifying all costs
and expenses therein against the lot, block, or parcel of land upon which such
building is situated, to the tax collector, and the same shall thereupon be a
lien as are other taxes, and the same shall be extended upon the tax rolls and
collected as other city taxes.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
   Ch. 226 S.L. 1947.
PUBLIC UTILITIES
SECTION 42(39). To allow, authorize, provide for and regulate the erection,
maintenance and removal of public utility or other poles, wires, and cables,
and the laying and using of underground conduits and subways for the same in,
under, upon, or over the streets, alleys, public parks, public places of said
city and any lands owned or under the control of said city, whether they be
inside the city limits or not; and to require all such wires and cables to be
laid in said conduits or subways when reasonably practicable.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
OFFICERS-COMPENSATION AND DUTIES
SECTION 42(40). To provide, either by Boise City, or by its, or some of its,
employees and officers, or by both, or by either or both through, with or in
cooperation with the state, United States, or governmental, insurance or other
agencies or corporations, for unemployment, old age, retirement, disability and
death (or any one or more thereof) payments or benefits to some or all city
employees and officers, and for the payment, or contributions to the payment,
of the cost thereof and for the establishment, accumulation and maintenance of
reserves and special funds therefor, and to levy special taxes therefor.
To establish and regulate the fees and compensation and to define the duties of
all officers in this municipal corporation. Provided, that no mayor or council
can, during their term of office, establish or regulate their own fees and
compensation, or the compensation and fees of their successors or any of them
within ten days before a general election.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
   Ch. 10 S.L. 1945.
CRIMINAL JURISDICTION
SECTION 42(41). To provide for the punishment of the violation of any of the
ordinances of the city by fine not exceeding three hundred dollars, or
imprisonment in the city jail, not exceeding sixty days, or both, or by a
forfeiture, as penalty, not exceeding three hundred dollars, and for working,
upon the streets, or public places any person sentenced to such imprisonment
during the term thereof, and to provide for the punishment of any person
sentenced to imprisonment who shall refuse to work when ordered.
   ANNOTATIONS:
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
   In re Snyder, 10 Ida. 688, 79 Pac. 821.
APPROPRIATIONS
SECTION 42(42). To appropriate money to pay the debts, liabilities and
expenditures of the city, or any part or item thereof. But no appropriations
shall be made in aid of any person, corporation or society, unless expressly
authorized by this Act or the laws of the state.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
DITCHES, DRAINAGE, SEWAGE, ETC.
SECTION 42(43). To locate, and construct any ditch, canal, or pipe for the
conduct of water, and any drain, sewage disposal facilities, sewer or culvert
it may deem necessary or convenient, and for such purposes shall have a right
to enter upon any land between the termini of the foregoing for the purpose of
examining, locating and surveying the foregoing, doing no unnecessary damage
thereby, and to appropriate so much of said land as may be necessary for the
construction and maintenance thereof in like manner as provided by the laws of
this state for the appropriation of lands or right of way by corporations, and
to appropriate and divert from its natural course or channel, for the purposes
of the city any spring or streams of water; and to compel the extension of
water and sewer connections from the main sewer or pipe to the curb line of the
sidewalks of all public streets.
   ANNOTATIONS:
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
   Wilson v. Boise City, 6 Ida. 397, 55 Pac. 889.
   Boise City v. Boise Rapid Transit Co., 6 Ida. 779, 59 Pac. 716.
   Boise Development Co., Ltd., v. Boise City, 30 Ida. 686, 167 Pac. 1034.
   Stephenson v. Pioneer Irr. Dist., 49 Ida. 195, 288 Pac. 423.
CHILDREN-EDUCATION
SECTION 42(44). To authorize the taking up, and provide for safe keeping and
education, for such periods of time as may be expedient, of all children who
are destitute of proper parental care.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
CENSUS-BURIALS-BIRTHS
SECTION 42(45). To provide for taking enumeration of the inhabitants of the
city, to regulate the burial of the dead, and keep a register of all births and
deaths; to direct the returning and keeping of all bills of mortality; and to
impose penalties on physicians, sextons and others for any default in the
premises.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1969.
HEALTH-NUISANCE
SECTION 42(46). For the preservation of the health of the inhabitants of the
city, said council and mayor are empowered to abate any nuisance outside of the
limits of the city affecting the health and comfort of the inhabitants thereof,
and in case of any such nuisance said council and mayor shall have the same
power as if such nuisance existed within the corporate limits of the city. They
shall also have jurisdiction over all places within five miles of the corporate
limits for the making and enforcement of any health or quarantine ordinance.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1989.
PUBLIC CARRIERS
SECTION 42(47). For the protection of life and property and the lessening of
danger thereto, to require all forms of transportation for hire within the city
to provide proper safety appliances, machinery, equipment, and methods,
including public liability and property damage bonds or insurance, and
otherwise to provide for the operation and licensing thereof, and to keep their
vehicles in comfortable and sanitary condition for the transportation of
passengers. Such regulations may be enforced by such fines and penalties as may
be by ordinance provided.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
SAME
SECTION 42(48). To regulate the moving and the operation, the time, the rate of
speed and rates of fare of all forms of transportation of persons or property
for hire within the city.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
REVENUE BONDS; WATER-SEWAGE-TREATMENT PLANTS-OFF-STREET PARKING
SECTION 42(49). To own, purchase, acquire, construct, reconstruct, better or
extend, equip, operate and maintain, within or without, or partially within or
partially without, or within any part of, the boundaries of Boise City, water
systems, sewage collection systems, water treatment plants, sewage treatment
plants, and off street parking facilities, or either or all of such systems or
facilities, and for the purpose of paying the cost thereof, may, with the
assent of two-thirds of the qualified electors voting at an election held for
that purpose, issue Revenue Bonds of the city for the payment thereof; to
prescribe and collect rates, fees, tolls, and charges for the services,
facilities and commodities furnished by such systems or facilities; to provide
methods for collection, and penalties, including denial of service, for
nonpayment of such rates, fees, tolls or charges. In addition to the foregoing,
and to exercise the powers and purposes herein provided, the Act cited as the
"Revenue Bond Act", and all of the provisions thereof, without limitation, and
as said Act may hereafter be amended from time to time, shall be applicable to
and shall apply to Boise City, said "Revenue Bond Act" being an Act enacted by
the Thirty-first Session of the Legislature of the state of Idaho as Senate
Bill No. 5.
   ANNOTATIONS:
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
   Ch. 115 S.L. 1951.
   Boise City v. Boise Artesian H. and C. Water Co., 186 Fed. 710 (decided
before 1951 amendment).
ISSUANCE OF BONDS
SECTION 42(50). Boise City shall have power and authority to borrow money and
issue therefor its negotiable bonds, with negotiable interest coupons attached,
not to exceed, at any time, in the aggregate, fifteen (15) percent of the value
of all taxable property in the said city, as shown by the last preceding
assessment list of said city, for any and all of the following purposes.
1.   To provide for the purchase or construction and maintenance of necessary
water works and supplying the same with water, and to provide for lights for
streets, public buildings and grounds.
2.   To provide for the laying, constructing, equipment and maintenance of
sewers, sewage disposal facilities, and drains.
3.   To provide for the improvement by any means or method, lighting,
beautifying, construction and laying out of streets and other highways, and the
purchase or condemnation of grounds therefor.
4.   To provide for funding, refunding, purchase and redemption of the
outstanding indebtedness of said city, either at this time or at any future
time.
5.   To provide for the purchase, construction, establishment and maintenance
of hospitals, pest houses and cemeteries, either within or without the
corporate limits of said city, and the purchase and acquisition of sites
therefor.
6.   To provide for the purchase, improvement, equipment and maintenance of
lands for the use of public parks and airports, either within or without the
corporate limits of said city.
7.   To provide for the purchase, construction, erection, and maintenance of
public buildings and the purchase or condemnation of building sites for the use
of said city: provided, that said city may join with the United States or its
agencies, the state of Idaho, or Ada County, or any other political subdivision
of the state of Idaho, in the purchase, erection, construction and furnishing
of a public building or improvement, and acquire sites, and issue bonds for the
proportion thereof, which shall be used and utilized by the said city.
8.   To provide for the establishment, equipment and maintenance of a fire
department, and for the purchase of suitable and necessary apparatus and
buildings, and building sites, for the use thereof, and for all other necessary
public improvements.
9.   To provide for acquiring, purchasing, constructing, operating and
maintaining gas and electric lighting plants, machinery and appliances, heating
and power plants; and for the acquisition, condemnation, purchase, maintenance
and operation of any other works, establishment, plants, machinery and things
for the use and service of the public and authorized by this Act to be
acquired, owned or operated by said city, including the property and plants of
any public service corporation taken over, under the terms of any franchise
authorized by this Act; and for the purpose of acquiring, purchasing or
condemning lands necessary as sites or locations for any of the buildings,
plants, utilities, or things which the city is authorized to own or operate.
10.   To provide necessary equipment for any municipal equipment department and
for any other general public and municipal purpose whatsoever authorized by the
terms of this Act, whether specifically referred to in this section or not, and
for the purpose of performing any duties, or discharging any functions or
obligations or exercising any power expressly or impliedly included in or
conferred by this Act, when so authorized by an election as herein provided
for.
Whenever the council of said city shall deem it advisable to issue negotiable
coupon bonds of said city, for any of the purposes aforesaid, the mayor and
council of said city shall provide therefor by ordinance, which shall specify
the purpose of issuing such proposed bonds; if it is to create new debt, the
object thereof must be stated, or, if it is to fund or refund any existing
indebtedness, it must be described; and when it consists of warrants or other
securities, they must be described by giving their number, date, and amount,
and the fund out of which the same, according to the terms thereof, are
payable; and the ordinance shall declare the purpose and total amount for which
such bonds shall be issued, and designate the provisions to be made to pay the
interest on such bonds as it falls due (but such ordinance need not state the
specific amount of interest), and also to constitute a sinking fund for the
payment of the principal thereof by amortized payments as elsewhere in this
charter provided or within twenty (20) years from the time of the issuance of
the same, and shall also provide for the holding of an election of the
qualified electors who are tax payers of such city, of which notice in general
terms shall be given by publication thereof at least three (3) times, at least
ten (10) days intervening between the first and last publication, in the
official newspaper of Boise City. Such election shall be conducted as other
city elections. One election may be held for the purpose of authorizing several
issues of bonds for different purposes, but the electors must be allowed to
vote upon each proposition severally. The voting at said election must be by
ballot, and the ballots used shall be substantially as follows: "In favor of
issuing bonds to the amount of               dollars for the purpose stated in
ordinance No.         ," and "Against issuing bonds to the amount of
            dollars for the purpose stated in ordinance No.      ." If at said
election, as provided for in this section, two-thirds (2/3) of the qualified
electors who are tax payers of such city, voting at said election, assent to
the issuing of said bonds, and the incurring of the indebtedness thereby
created for the purpose aforesaid, such bonds so authorized for said purposes
shall be issued in the manner hereinafter provided.
Such bonds shall be known as municipal coupon bonds of Boise City, and shall be
issued in denominations of not more than one thousand ($1,000.00) dollars and
not less than one hundred ($100.00) dollars each, as the mayor and council may
determine. Such bonds shall be made payable within twenty (20) years from the
date of issue thereof. The bonds must bear interest at such rate not exceeding
six (6) percent per annum, as the mayor and council may determine, to be paid
semi-annually in each year, at the office of the city treasurer, or at any
banking house or trust company in the United States, which may be designated by
the mayor and council. Such bonds shall be redeemable at the pleasure of said
city at any time after the expiration of ten (10) years from the date of
issuance thereof, and each bond must be redeemable in the order it is numbered.
The bonds mentioned in this section must have attached thereto, when
negotiated, semi-annual interest coupons covering the interest expressed in the
bonds from the date of issuance until paid. Such bonds must be signed by the
mayor and attested by the city clerk of the city, and bear the seal of the
city, and countersigned by the treasurer thereof, and the coupons attached to
such bonds must be signed by the said treasurer. The signature of the treasurer
to such coupons may be lithographed. Each coupon must have annexed to the same
a number corresponding with the number of the bond, and each bond must state
upon its face the amount for which it was issued, and the date of issue, and be
made payable to person named or to bearer, and must recite that it is issued by
virtue of and in conformity and compliance with the provisions of this Act, and
of the constitution and laws of the state of Idaho.
The mayor and council must cause notice to be given by the clerk by publication
for at least once in each of two (2) consecutive weeks in the official
newspaper of said city of its intention to issue and negotiate such bonds, and
invite bidders therefor, and after ascertaining the best terms upon which such
bonds can be negotiated, must secure the proper engraving or printing thereof
and thereafter have them consecutively numbered, properly prepared and
executed. Any and all bids may be rejected, or the bonds may be offered in
several lots or blocks; and all bonds may be readvertised and reoffered from
time to time, until said bids are procured; when the bonds are executed, they
must be, by the city clerk of said city, registered in a public record book, to
be kept for that purpose, and therein must be stated the name of the purchaser,
and the number, date, and amount of each bond, time, place of payment, rate of
interest, number of coupons attached, and any other proper description thereof,
for future identification.
Then the mayor and council must direct the city clerk, from time to time, in
such amounts as they deem best, to deliver such bonds to the treasurer of said
city, and take and file his receipts therefor and charge him therewith; any
duties relating to bonds required of said mayor and council may be performed at
any meeting thereof, however held. The said treasurer must, under the
supervision of the city clerk, deliver such bonds to the purchaser or
purchasers thereof, and in no case must such bonds be sold for less than their
face or par value, and the accrued interest at the time of delivery. Such bonds
may be delivered, in case of funding or refunding, in exchange for or on
cancellation of any equal amount of prior indebtedness being funded or
refunded, or for cash. All proceedings for the issuance and sale, and the sale
of funding or refunding bonds may be had prior to the callable date of bonds to
be funded or refunded. All proceeds derived from the sale of such bonds must be
applied exclusively to the purposes for which the bonds are issued.
The city treasurer must keep a record of all bonds disposed of, showing their
number, rate of interest, date, and amount of sale, and when and where payable,
and the name and address of the purchasers, which record must be kept open for
the inspection of the public at all reasonable office hours - and he must make
detailed statements to the mayor and council or city clerk of all his
transactions under the provisions of this section, as often as required.
The mayor and council must, upon the issue of such bonds, by ordinance, direct
to be levied, and must thereafter levy annually, upon all taxable property of
said city, a sufficient sum to pay the interest on all bonds disposed of under
this section, as it falls due, and after such bonds have been issued for a
period of ten (10) years, they must levy in addition annually a sufficient sum
to constitute a sinking fund for the payment of one-tenth (1/10) of the
principal of such bonds. And all such taxes must be levied, assessed and
collected as other city taxes, until the bonds so issued are fully paid,
including the interest thereon.
The faith, credit and all taxable property within the limits of said city, as
they now exist or may hereafter be extended, are and must continue pledged, and
the proper officers of said city must continue to assess and collect on all
taxable property within the limits thereof, the necessary taxes to pay said
bonds and interest as the same become due. Should the tax for the payment of
interest on or the principal of bonds issued under the provisions of this
section at any time not be collected in time to meet such payment, the money
must be paid out of any moneys in the general fund of the city, and the money
so used for such payment must be repaid to the fund from which so taken, out of
the first moneys paid therein, and a sum, sufficient to cover such deficit
shall be levied and collected in the next, or any succeeding year. It shall be
the duty of said treasurer, in case of the sale of said bonds, to use the
proceeds arising from the sale thereof in payment of the indebtedness described
in said ordinance only. Any failure of any officers of said city to comply with
any of the provisions of this section shall be termed a misdemeanor, and any
such officer shall be fined an amount not exceeding the sum of two hundred
dollars ($200.00), or imprisoned in the city jail not exceeding sixty days.
No bond issued under the provision of this charter shall be invalidated,
annulled, or set aside on account of any defect, irregularity, omission,
informality, failure to comply with the charter, provisions, or other act or
thing whatsoever, unless by reason thereof it shall appear to the court that a
substantial injury has been or is about to be suffered by the property owners
and tax payers of said city, it being the intent of this Act that bond issues
shall rest upon the consent of the tax payers, and that credit of the city
shall not be injured by the cancellation of securities when issued.
The mayor and council may recite in such bonds that all acts and things
requisite to the issue thereof have been duly and regularly performed and fully
complied with, and that the same are duly and regularly issued, and, as
affecting innocent purchasers, such recitals shall be conclusive.
That in all cases where municipal coupon bonds, which have been issued under
any general law in the state of Idaho for any purpose set forth in said general
law, have been heretofore or may hereafter be declared invalid or void by any
order or decree of court, the mayor and common council of Boise City, Idaho,
are hereby authorized and empowered to provide for the reissuance of said bonds
in such amounts as will cover the principal and interest due on said bonds
declared to be invalid or void.
   ANNOTATIONS:
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
   Boise City National Bank v. Boise City, 15 Ida. 796, 100 Pac. 94.
   Swain v. Fritchman, 21 Ida. 805, 125 Pac. 327.
   Russell v. Boise City, 70 Ida. 199, 214 P.(2) 472.
LIMITATION OF CRIMINAL JURISDICTION
SECTION 42(51). The power and authority granted by Section 42(41) can only be
enforced or exercised by ordinance, unless otherwise expressly provided; and a
majority of the council may pass any ordinance or resolution not repugnant to
the constitution and laws of the United States or of the state of Idaho,
necessary or convenient for carrying into effect any power or authority granted
by this Act.
   ANNOTATIONS:
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
   In re Ridenbaugh, 5 Ida. 374, 49 Pac. 13.
   In re Snyder, 10 Ida. 688, 79 Pac. 821.
   Mix v. Board of County Commissioners (Lewiston), 18 Ida. 704, 112 Pac. 218.
BUILDINGS-REGULATION
SECTION 42(52). For the purpose of promoting health, safety, morals, or the
general welfare of Boise City, the council shall have the power to regulate and
restrict the height, number of stories and size of buildings and other
structures, the percentage of lot that may be occupied, the size of yard,
courts, and open spaces, the density of population, and the location and use of
buildings, structures and lands for trade, industry, residence, or other
purposes, as provided by ordinance.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
NARCOTICS
SECTION 42(53). To prohibit and regulate by ordinance the sale, manufacture for
sale, transportation for sale, furnishing or giving to any person or persons
within Boise City any cocaine, alpha or beta eucaine, opium, morphine, heroin,
choral hydrate, marihuana, marijuana, or griffo, or any salt or compound of any
of the foregoing substances, or any preparation or compound containing any of
the foregoing substances or their salts or compounds, and to provide for the
lawful disposition thereof, and the punishment for violation of any ordinance
adopted pursuant to the power herein granted.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
LOCAL IMPROVEMENTS-SUPERVISION
SECTION 42(54). In making any general or local improvement herein authorized to
be made by the city and paid for in full by the city, or to be paid for and
assessed against property owners, as herein provided, if in the opinion of the
city council said work can be done cheaper and better by the city itself than
under contract, the city council shall have power to do and perform said work,
or cause the same to be done under its supervision, instead of letting the same
to be done by contract.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
WEEDS-SNOW AND ICE-TREES
SECTION 42(55). To provide by ordinance for the destruction and extermination
of noxious weeds, the clearing from sidewalks of snow and ice, and the spraying
and caring for trees, and the entering upon private premises to accomplish said
purposes, and levy and collect taxes against the property upon which such labor
is performed.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
CONTRACTS WITH FIRE ASSOCIATIONS
SECTION 42(56). The mayor and city council shall have power to enter into
contracts, and do any and all other things necessary in order to completely
cooperate with cooperative associations or corporations organized under the
laws of Idaho for protection of property of members from fire; to purchase and
maintain fire fighting equipment and employ firemen in connection therewith; to
authorize the sending of fire fighting equipment and firemen employed by the
city of Boise to the property of the members of said cooperative associations
or corporations; to appropriate money therefor.
   Ch. 216 S.L. 1939.
AIRPORTS-BONDS
SECTION 42-A. The mayor and common council shall have power: To acquire by
condemnation or otherwise, establish, purchase and improve, aviation fields and
airports, and for that purpose to purchase, improve, equip and maintain lands,
either within or without the corporate limits of said city, and Boise City
shall have the power and authority to borrow money and issue therefor its
negotiable bonds with negotiable interest coupons attached for any of the above
mentioned purposes, said bonds to be issued substantially in the same manner as
provided in subsection 50 of Section 42, of the said Boise City charter,
provided that said bonds shall not exceed in the aggregate with all other bonds
issued by the city pursuant to the provisions of said subsection 50 of Section
42 of said Boise City charter fifteen percent of the value of all taxable
property in the said city as shown by the last preceding assessment list of
said city.
   Ch. 241 S.L. 1929.
REFUNDING INDEBTEDNESS
SECTION 42-B. The mayor and common council shall have power to issue bonds
under paragraph 4, Section 42(50) of the charter of Boise City for the purpose
of funding, refunding, purchase or redemption of the outstanding indebtedness
of Boise City, other than warrants, when the same can be done to the profit and
benefit of the city and without incurring any additional liability, without the
submission of the question of such bonds to the electors of the city.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
AMORTIZATION OF BONDS
SECTION 42-C. Whenever bonds are issued under any provisions of the charter of
Boise City they may at the option of the common council of said city, be made
to mature and be payable upon an annual amortization plan. The first annual
amortized principal payment shall mature and be payable at the expiration of
two years from and after the date of issue and the various annual maturities
shall as nearly as practical be in such principal amounts as will, together
with the accruing interest on all outstanding bonds of such issue, be met and
paid by an equal annual tax levy for the payment of the principal of said bonds
and interest thereon during the term for which such bonds shall be issued.
Provided that it shall not be necessary to prescribe such amortized annual
maturities in any bond issue until the interest rate to be borne by such bonds
shall have been ascertained upon and after the sale thereof.
   Ch. 102 S.L. 1931. Ch. 3 S.L. 1945.
AIRPORTS-OPERATION-MAINTENANCE-REGULATION
SECTION 42-D. Boise City, acting by its mayor and common council, shall have
power:
1.   To improve, maintain, operate, manage and control any and all such
aviation fields, airports and real and personal property used therefor or in
connection therewith as are now or hereafter owned or possessed by Boise City;
2.   To construct or otherwise acquire, install, own, hold, operate, maintain,
manage and control on, adjacent to, or in connection with such aviation fields,
airports, or property used therefor or in connection therewith, such hangars,
repair shops, depots, gasoline stations, buildings and other structures and
such equipment as may be necessary or convenient for the operation or
maintenance of such aviation fields or airports;
3.   To make and enforce ordinances, rules or regulations for the operation,
management, regulation, control and use of all such aviation fields, airports,
hangars, repair shops, depots, gasoline stations, buildings, structures,
improvements, equipment and other property as are above mentioned, and to
establish, charge and collect fees or rentals for the use of the same or any
part thereof;
4.   To make contracts granting rights to the use of such aviation fields and
airports, together with the lighting systems and similar equipment therefor,
for aviation purposes in common with other users;
5.   To lease for aviation purposes or purposes connected with or incidental
thereto, the hangars, hangar space, repair shops, depots, gasoline stations,
buildings and similar property belonging to or possessed by Boise City and used
in connection with such aviation fields or airports; and,
6.   To lease such parts of said aviation fields, airports and the real estate
used therefor or in connection therewith, as the mayor and common council may
deem advisable for the construction, maintenance, operation and/or occupancy of
hangars, repair shops, passenger and freight depots, gasoline stations,
restaurants, refreshment stands or for similar purposes connected with or
incidental to the maintenance and operation of such aviation fields and
airports.
Contracts and leases made under one or more of subdivisions 4, 5 and 6 hereof
shall be made for such rental or other consideration and for such length of
time and upon such other terms and conditions as said mayor and common council
in their discretion may determine, provided, however, that with the exception
of rights granted by lease under subdivisions 5 and 6 hereof, no right to the
exclusive use of any airport, aviation field or other property above mentioned
or any part thereof shall ever be granted or created, nor with the exception of
property leased under subdivisions 5 and 6 hereof shall the possession,
management, operation or control of such aviation fields, airport, or other
property or any part thereof be transferred or surrendered by the city to
anyone.
   Ch. 142 S.L. 1931.
TAX ANTICIPATION BONDS OR NOTES
SECTION 42-D. SUBSECTION A. The mayor and common council of Boise City shall
have the power from time to time, by resolution, to borrow money and to issue
tax anticipation bonds or notes, bearing interest at such rate not exceeding
six percent per annum as may be determined by the mayor and common council, and
maturing not more than one year from the date thereof, for the purpose of
providing funds in anticipation of the collection of taxes of the current
fiscal year in which said tax anticipation bonds or notes are issued, exclusive
of taxes required to be raised to pay the principal of outstanding bonded
indebtedness of Boise City, the proceeds of such bonds or notes to be used for
the purpose for which said taxes are levied. The amount authorized to be
borrowed by means of such tax anticipation bonds or notes shall not exceed
seventy-five percent of the taxes levied for the current fiscal year and not
yet collected by said Boise City. If the tax levy for the fiscal year has not
been computed, then the amount of tax anticipation bonds or notes issued in
anticipation of taxes to be levied for such fiscal year shall not exceed
seventy-five percent of the taxes levied by said Boise City in the previous
fiscal year. In determining the amount of tax anticipation bonds or notes which
may be issued, the mayor and common council shall declare in the resolution
providing for the issuance of such bonds or notes the amount of taxes levied
for the current fiscal year and the amount of such taxes not yet collected by
Boise City, or in the event that the tax levy for the fiscal year has not been
completed, the mayor and common council shall declare in the resolution
providing for the issuance of such tax anticipation bonds or notes the amount
of taxes levied by the said Boise City in the previous fiscal year. In each
instance, taxes raised or to be raised to pay the principal of outstanding
bonded indebtedness of the said Boise City shall not be included in the amount
of taxes against which such tax anticipation bonds or notes are authorized to
be issued. Such tax anticipation bonds or notes shall be negotiable
instruments, and the full faith, credit and resources of Boise City shall be
pledged for the payment of the same. Such bonds or notes shall be issued in
such form and detail as shall be determined by the mayor and common council of
Boise City by resolution duly adopted.
SUBSECTION B. Such tax anticipation bonds or notes may be sold at public or
private sale at such times, in such amounts and on such terms as may be
determined by the mayor and common council.
SUBSECTION C. To provide for the payment of said tax anticipation bonds or
notes at maturity, there shall be created by the resolution providing for the
issuance of said tax anticipation bonds or notes a special fund to be known as
the "Tax Anticipation Bond or Note Redemption Fund." Whenever any tax
anticipation bonds or notes have been issued in anticipation of the collection
of taxes, all such taxes thereafter collected or received, the collection of
which has been so anticipated, shall be placed in the "Tax Anticipation Bond or
Note Redemption Fund" until such time as the funds accumulated therein shall be
sufficient to pay all such tax anticipation bonds or notes outstanding,
together with interest thereon at maturity, and the funds so accumulated in the
"Tax Anticipation Bond or Note Redemption Fund" are hereby appropriated and set
apart for such purpose only, and shall be used for no other purpose; provided,
however, that nothing in this section shall be construed to limit the payment
of the principal of and interest on said tax anticipation bonds or notes solely
to the taxes, in anticipation of which said bonds or notes were issued, but
such bonds or notes shall be the direct and general obligation of Boise City.
SUBSECTION D. In the event that the taxes collected for any fiscal year prior
to date on which final installment of such taxes becomes delinquent shall not
be sufficient to pay the tax anticipation bonds or notes issued in anticipation
of the collection of taxes of such fiscal year, the said Boise City shall in
providing for the levy of taxes for the succeeding fiscal year, include in such
tax levy for the succeeding fiscal year the amount necessary to cover such
deficiency in the collection of such taxes, such levy in the succeeding year to
be in an amount which, together with the amount of taxes then in such "Tax
Anticipation Bond or Note Redemption Fund" shall be sufficient to provide for
the payment of principal of and interest on the tax anticipation bonds or notes
issued in anticipation of such taxes and payable out of such fund.
SUBSECTION E. Boise City shall have the power to issue refunding bonds or
notes, with like limitations upon interest and maturity, and shall issue
refunding bonds or notes where such refunding bonds or notes shall be necessary
to provide for the payment of any tax anticipation bonds or notes at maturity,
or to provide for the payment of any tax anticipation bonds or notes heretofore
issued by Boise City where such tax anticipation bonds or notes are outstanding
and unpaid after their maturity date. Said refunding bonds or notes shall be
authorized by resolution and shall be issued, sold and paid as herein provided
for the issuance, sale and payment of tax anticipation bonds or notes. At no
time shall the total amount outstanding of such tax anticipation bonds or notes
and such refunding bonds or notes exceed seventy-five percent of the amount of
taxes levied for the current fiscal year and not yet collected by said Boise
City, or if such refunding bonds or notes are issued before the tax levy for
any fiscal year has been completed, then the total amount outstanding of such
tax anticipation bonds or notes and such refunding bonds or notes shall not
exceed seventy-five percent of the amount of taxes levied by said Boise City in
the previous fiscal year; provided that where refunding bonds or notes have
been issued or the issuance thereof has been provided for by the adoption of a
resolution for the purpose of refunding any tax anticipation bonds or notes,
the said tax anticipation bonds or notes to be refunded by said refunding bonds
or notes shall not be included in determining the total amount of tax
anticipation bonds and notes outstanding, but for that purpose shall be treated
as having been refunded and retired by such refunding bonds or notes.
SUBSECTION F. This Act shall be construed as full authority for the issuance of
such tax anticipation bonds or notes, and it shall not be necessary to comply
with the requirements or provisions of any other section or provision of Boise
City charter as amended, relative to the issuance or sale of bonds or notes of
Boise City in connection with the issuance of tax anticipation bonds or notes
issued under the authority of this Act.
SUBSECTION G. In order to carry out the provisions of this Act, all necessary
actions are hereby authorized and directed.
   Ch. 63 S.L. 1935.
GRANT OF REAL PROPERTY
SECTION 42-E. To grant, convey, give, or cede to any school district, junior
college district, or any municipal subdivision, any of the real property of
Boise City, upon such terms and conditions as may be approved by the mayor and
common council of said city.
   Ch. 221 S.L. 1939.
BONDS OF OFFICERS
SECTION 42-F. The mayor and common council of Boise City shall require a
separate annual surety bond for the term of each fiscal year to be furnished by
the city clerk and city treasury in such amounts as in the judgment of the
mayor and council may seem proper, and may, at their option, require a like
surety bond from such other officers and employees of the municipality, in such
amounts and from such officers and employees as in the judgment of the mayor
and council may seem proper. The premium on any bond furnished pursuant to the
requirements of this section shall be paid by the municipality.
   Ch. 31 S.L. 1941.
SCOPE OF PRECEDING SECTION
SECTION 43. The foregoing or other enumeration of particular powers granted by
this Act, shall not be construed to impair any general grant of power herein
contained, nor to limit any such general grant to powers of the same class or
classes as those so enumerated.
   S.L. 1907, p. 78.
ADVERTISING-HOW LET
SECTION 44. The council shall, on or after the first Monday in May each year,
let the legal advertising of the city to a person, firm, copartnership or
corporation publishing, for at least six (6) days each week, a newspaper of
general circulation within the city of Boise, which makes the lowest and best
bid therefor, and said bidder shall give a bond to the city, in such sum as may
be fixed by the council, to well and faithfully perform the conditions of the
contract. It shall be the duty of the council to designate a newspaper or the
newspapers published by the bidder receiving such contract and giving such bond
as the official newspaper or newspapers of the city. All the legal advertising
of the city during the term of such contract shall be printed in one or more of
such official newspapers. Whenever in this charter publication is required for
any number of weeks it shall be sufficient to publish in one issue each week on
the same day of the week. All ordinances adopted for the purpose of granting a
franchise shall be printed with seven and one-half (7½) point type or larger.
   Ch. 215 S.L. 1939.
QUARTERLY STATEMENTS
SECTION 45. It shall be the duty of the mayor of Boise City to cause to be
published in some newspaper published in said city, quarterly statements of the
financial condition of said city, showing the amounts received and disbursed in
each quarter, and the actual indebtedness of the city at the end of such
quarter, including both floating and bonded indebtedness. Such statement shall
be verified by the certificate under oath of the city clerk and ex-officio
auditor.
   S.L. 1907, pp. 78-79.
ORDINANCE-STYLE-RECORDING
SECTION 46. The style of every ordinance shall be: "Boise City does ordain as
follows:" Every ordinance after its passage shall be recorded in a book kept
for that purpose, which record shall be authenticated by the president of the
council and attested by the city clerk, and in case such ordinance is approved
by the mayor, he shall also sign such record.
   ANNOTATIONS:
   S.L. 1907, p. 79.
   State v. Calloway, 11 Ida. 719, 84 Pac. 27.
LOCAL IMPROVEMENT DISTRICT CODE
SECTION 48. Chapter 25 of title 49 of the Idaho Code Annotated, cited as the
"Local Improvement District Code" and all of the provisions thereof, shall be
applicable and shall apply to Boise City and in addition thereto Section 48-
A and Section 48-B of this charter shall be applicable to and be deemed a part
of the "Local Improvement District Code" of Boise City.
   ANNOTATIONS:
   Ch. 31 S.L. 1941.
   Boise City National Bank v. Boise City, 15 Ida. 792, 100 Pac. 93.
   Lusk v. Boise City, 50 Ida. 50, 292 Pac. 1100.
   Maguire v. Whillock, 63 Ida. 630, 124 P.(2) 248.
   Cruzen v. Boise City, 58 Ida. 406, 74 P.(2) 1037.
   (The above cases decided before 1941 amendment.)
LIEN OF LOCAL IMPROVEMENT DISTRICT BONDS
SECTION 48-A. All local improvement district bonds issued by Boise City under
the provisions of the "Local Improvement District Code" shall be equal liens
upon all the property within the local improvement district for the assessments
represented by such bonds without priority of one over another to the extent of
the several assessments against the several lots and parcels of land.
   ANNOTATION:
   Ch. 31 S.L. 1941.
   Russell v. Boise City, 70 Ida. 199, 214 P.(2) 472.
PAYMENT OF LOCAL IMPROVEMENT DISTRICT ASSESSMENTS IN INSTALLMENTS
SECTION 48-B. The common council may, in lieu of the issuance of bonds as
provided by the "Local Improvement District Code", as its option, provide for
the payment of any assessments against property within any local improvement
district, in annual or semi-annual installments, the last of which said
installment payments must be payable not more than 5 years from the date of
confirmation of the assessment roll by the common council.
   Ch. 31 S.L. 1941. Ch. 226 S.L. 1947.
MAYOR-QUALIFICATIONS-DUTIES
SECTION 49.1. The chief executive officer of Boise City shall be designated the
mayor. He shall be at least thirty years old, and having had the qualifications
of an elector of the municipality for the five years next preceding the day of
his election. He shall preside over the council when in session, and shall have
authority to preserve order, enforce the rules of the council and determine the
order of business, subject to such rules and to appeal to the council. He shall
not be entitled to a vote, except in case of a tie, when he shall have the
deciding vote.
   Ch. 31 S.L. 1941.
VETO-PASSING OVER
SECTION 49.2. The mayor may veto any ordinance or resolution passed by the
council or any authorization for the payment of money authorized by the council
within 3 days after the same is passed or authorized, and it shall require a
three-fourths vote of the whole council within 30 days after receiving the
mayor's veto to pass such ordinance, resolution or authorization.
   Ch. 31 S.L. 1941.
UNDERTAKINGS
SECTION 49.3. The mayor shall take and approve all official undertakings which
this Act or any ordinance of the city may require any officer or employee to
give as security for the faithful performance of his duty, or any undertaking
which may be required of any contractor for the faithful performance of his
contract; and when he approves such undertakings he must immediately file the
same with the city clerk excepting the undertaking of the city clerk, of which
he shall be the custodian.
   Ch. 31 S.L. 1941.
DISBURSEMENTS AND ORDINANCES-APPROVED BY MAYOR
SECTION 49.4. No resolution or authorization for the payment of money, nor any
ordinance, shall go into force or be of any effect until approved by the mayor,
except as provided in Section 49.5.
   Ch. 31 S.L. 1941.
ORDINANCES-FAILURE OF MAYOR TO APPROVE
SECTION 49.5. All ordinances, resolutions and authorizations for the payment of
money, passed by the common council of Boise City, shall be transmitted by the
city clerk to the mayor within 12 hours after their passage or approval. If the
mayor does not approve such resolution, authorization for the payment of money,
or any ordinance so transmitted, he must, within three days from the receipt
thereof, return the same to the city clerk with his reason in writing for not
approving the same, who shall transmit such ordinance, resolution or
authorization, together with the mayor's reasons for disapproving the same, to
the common council at or prior to its next regular meeting, and if the mayor
does not so return such resolution, authorization or ordinance, the same shall
become a law, and shall take effect as if he had approved the same.
   Ch. 31 S.L. 1941.
MAYOR-DUTIES
SECTION 49.6. The mayor shall vigilantly observe the conduct of all public
officers and employees, and take notice of the degree of fidelity with which
they execute their duties and obligations, especially in the collection,
custody, administration and disbursement of the public funds and property. He
shall take special care to see that all the books and records of Boise City
departments, boards and officers, are kept in legal and proper form, and any
defalcation or wilful neglect of duty, or any official misconduct which he may
discover or which he may be cognizant of shall be laid by him before the common
council and city attorney, in order that the public interest may be protected,
and the person in default be proceeded against according to law. He shall see
that the ordinances of Boise City are observed and enforced.
   Ch. 31 S.L. 1941.
RIOTS AND TUMULTS
SECTION 49.7. He shall take all proper measures for the preservation of the
public order and suppression of all riots and tumults.
   Ch. 31 S.L. 1941.
LEGAL PROCEEDINGS
SECTION 49.8. He shall see that all contracts and agreements with Boise City
are faithfully kept and fully performed; and to that end shall cause legal
proceedings to be commenced and prosecuted in the name of Boise City against
all persons or corporations failing to fulfill their agreements on contracts,
either in whole or in part.
OFFICE HOURS
SECTION 49.9. The mayor shall have regular office hours at the city hall for
the transaction of the public business.
   Ch. 31 S.L. 1941.
ORDINANCES-APPROVAL OF PART
SECTION 49.10. In case an ordinance or resolution of the council shall
appropriate money, the mayor may approve one or more of the items in such
ordinance or resolution and disapprove another or others as provided in Section
49.5. Those which he approves and those which he fails to disapprove shall
become effective, and those which he shall disapprove shall become effective
only when again passed by a three-fourths vote of the council, as herein
provided in case of a veto upon other matters.
   Ch. 31 S.L. 1941.
WARRANTS-HOW SIGNED
SECTION 49.11. All warrants on the treasury shall be signed by the mayor and
countersigned by the city clerk and ex-officio auditor.
   Ch. 31 S.L. 1941.
ATTORNEY-QUALIFICATIONS-DUTIES
SECTION 50. The city attorney shall have been a qualified elector of the city
for at least one year before his appointment. He shall have been duly admitted
to practice in the Supreme Court of Idaho, and shall have been actually engaged
in the practice of his profession for a period of at least three years before
his appointment. It shall be his duty to promptly and carefully attend to all
suits and other matters in which the city maybe legally interested; to give his
advice and opinion, in writing, whenever required in writing, by the mayor,
common council, any department or city officer. He shall be the legal adviser
of all city officers; he shall draft or approve the form of all official or
other bonds given to the city; and all contracts made with the city; he shall
draft, whenever requested, by the mayor or common council or any member
thereof, any proposed ordinance or resolution or order of the common council
and shall do and perform all other things touching his office required of him
by the mayor or common council.
   S.L. 1907, p. 83.
STREET COMMISSIONER-DUTIES
SECTION 51. There is hereby established an executive department of the
municipal government of the city which shall be known as the department of
public works, which department shall include: (1) the bureau of engineering,
which shall include a division of maps and plats and a division of sewers; (2)
the bureau of sewage disposal; (3) the bureau of waste disposal; and (4) the
bureau of streets, rivers and gulches. All officers and employees of each of
said bureaus shall be under the direction and supervision of the commissioner
of public works.
   Ch. 41 S.L. 1949.
ENGINEER-QUALIFICATIONS-DUTIES
SECTION 52(1). The commissioner of public works shall be a licensed
professional engineer under the laws of the state of Idaho. He shall have such
duties as may be prescribed by ordinance and shall have superintendence: of all
public construction and improvements; of the construction, improvement, repair,
improvement and maintenance of all streets, alleys, highways, walks, curbs,
gutters, bridges and viaducts of the city; of all works of the city for flood
control and drainage of surface or subterranean waters; of all sewers and
sewage disposal facilities; of all garbage and waste disposal; of all functions
prescribed by this charter for all bureaus included within the department of
public works.
SECTION 52(2). The bureau of engineering shall have such duties and functions
as may be prescribed by ordinance and shall have jurisdiction of:
1.   All engineering matters, except as otherwise in this charter provided,
pertaining to construction and maintenance within the jurisdiction of the
department of public works;
2.   All maps and plats of the city relating to all streets, alleys and public
ways of the city, and all works or facilities on, over or under the same; maps
and plats of the city relating to water courses, and drainage within the city;
plans and blueprints of public buildings and facilities of the city; and all
maps and plats of the city pertaining to the geographic or topographic aspects
of the city;
3.   The construction, maintenance, repair and control of all sewers and
drainage facilities of, or within, the city.
SECTION 52(3). The bureau of waste disposal shall have such duties and
functions as may be prescribed by ordinance and shall have jurisdiction over
the collection and disposal of all trash, rubbish and garbage.
SECTION 52(4). The bureau of sewage disposal shall have charge of the
maintenance, repair and upkeep of all sanitary sewage disposal facilities of
the city.
SECTION 52(5). The bureau of streets, rivers and gulches shall have such duties
as may be prescribed by ordinance and shall have charge over all construction,
maintenance, repair and improvement of all streets, alleys, highways, walks,
curbs, gutters, bridges and viaducts, and the control and maintenance of all
waterways under the jurisdiction or control of the department of public works.
   Ch. 41 S.L. 1949.
CLERK-DUTIES
SECTION 53. 1. It shall be the duty of the city clerk to attend all meetings of
the council and keep an accurate record of all their proceedings. He shall be
custodian of the corporate seal of the city and of all the municipal books,
records and papers, except as the custody of the same is not herein otherwise
provided for. He shall have full power and authority to take all affidavits and
administer all oaths necessary in the transaction of city business, but shall
make no charge therefor. His official books and records shall be kept properly
indexed and be open to public inspection during office hours.
2.   He shall be the general accountant of the city, and shall keep a complete
set of books for that purpose. Such books shall exhibit accurate and detailed
statements of all moneys received and expended for account of the city and of
the property owned by the city, and the income, if any, derived therefrom. He
shall keep separate accounts of each appropriation, and of the dates, purpose
and manner of each payment therefrom.
3.   He shall issue all licenses, and keep a classified record of the same,
showing date of issuance and expiration, class and amount. He must draw
warrants on the city treasurer in favor of all persons entitled thereto, in
payment of all claims and demands chargeable against the city, which have been
legally examined and allowed, as herein provided; also for all debts and
demands against the city when the amounts are fixed by law or ordinance. All
warrants must distinctly specify the liability for which they are drawn, and
when it accrued.
4.   He shall draw and countersign all warrants on the treasury, and no payment
of city funds shall be made except on draft or warrant countersigned by him. He
shall not countersign any such draft or warrant until he has found that the
payment has been legally authorized, that the money therefor has been duly
appropriated, and that such appropriation has not been exhausted.
5.   He shall perform such duties required of him by ordinance as may not be
inconsistent with the duties of his office.
6.   He shall report to the council monthly the actual condition of each fund
in the treasury, and make generally a specific exhibit of the city's financial
condition. He shall also make an annual report, showing in detail the source
from which the city's resources were derived and how much revenues were
expended for the preceding fiscal year, as well as showing in summarized form
the city's assets and indebtedness of all kinds. He shall give full information
as to the actual condition of the city treasury and every fund thereof,
whenever required by the mayor or common council, or any member thereof. All
such reports of said clerk are to be verified under oath.
   S.L. 1907, pp. 85-86.
TREASURER-DUTIES
SECTION 54. 1. The treasurer shall receive and keep all moneys that shall come
to the city by taxation or otherwise, and pay out the same only upon the
warrant of the mayor countersigned by the auditor. He shall keep an account
with the general fund and a separate account with each special fund that may be
raised for any specific object, and when a warrant is drawn on any particular
fund, it shall be paid out of such fund only.
2.   He shall make a sworn monthly statement to the council showing the
receipts and disbursements for the preceding months, and the state of each
particular fund, at the close of business on the last day of such month, and
also an annual report summarizing such matters for the whole year.
3.   He shall be in personal attendance at his office each day during office
hours. No fees of any kind shall be retained by him, but the same, from
whatever source received or derived shall be paid by him into the treasury. He
shall do and perform such other duties as may be prescribed by ordinance,
touching his office and not inconsistent therewith.
   S.L. 1907, p. 86.
CHIEF OF POLICE-DUTIES
SECTION 55. 1. The chief of police, for the suppression of any riot, public
tumult, disturbance of the public peace, or any organized resistance against
the laws or public authorities in the lawful execution of their functions,
shall have the powers that are now or may be hereafter conferred upon sheriffs
by the laws of this state; and his lawful orders shall be promptly executed by
police officers and watchmen in the city.
2.   He shall execute and return all process issued and directed to him by any
legal authority. He shall enforce all ordinances of the city and arrest all
persons guilty of violation of the same, or at once report the fact of such
violation to the mayor.
3.   He shall have charge of the city prison and prisoners confined therein,
and all those who are sentenced to labor upon the streets or public works, and
shall see that all orders and sentences in reference thereto are fully executed
and complied with, and shall perform such other duties as may be prescribed by
the mayor and common council.
   S.L. 1907, pp. 86-87.
MUNICIPAL COURT-MAGISTRATE JURISDICTION-DUTIES
SECTION 57. 1. The judicial power of the city shall be vested in a municipal
court and the judge thereof, to be known as the city magistrate, who shall be
not less than thirty years of age at the time of his appointment, and a
qualified elector of the city for three years immediately preceding such
appointment.
2.   The municipal court shall always be open for the transaction of business,
except on legal holidays. The judge thereof shall have the power to enforce due
obedience to all orders, rules, judgments and decrees made by him, and may fine
or imprison for contempt offered to such judge while holding his court, or to
process issued by him, in the same manner and to the same extent as the
district court.
3.   The municipal court shall have exclusive jurisdiction in all matters of
violations of the city ordinances. It shall have original jurisdiction of all
actions brought to recover or enforce any forfeiture or penalty declared by any
city ordinance, where the amount involved does not exceed $500.
4.   The salary of the city magistrate shall be his only compensation for
services rendered in that office. All fees or compensation received by him the
conduct of his office other than such salary shall be by him accounted for at
the end of every month, to the city auditor, and paid over to the city
treasurer.
5.   Appeals may be taken and shall be allowed from final judgments rendered in
the municipal court in all actions, in the same manner and with like effect,
that appeals may be taken and shall be allowed from final judgments rendered in
justices' courts.
   S.L. 1907, p. 88.
PURCHASING SUPPLIES
SECTION 58. Supplies, materials, equipment or construction for an amount
exceeding $100.00 shall not be ordered, purchased, or made by any officer,
board or department of the municipality authorized to incur any expenditure,
except after the council shall receive bids or proposals and award the contract
or purchase to the bidder who, in the judgment of the council, offers the item
or items in the quantity, quality, kind or design most suitable to the needs of
the municipality at the lowest and best bid.
   Ch. 81 S.L. 1941.
AUDITING COMMITTEE-DUTIES
SECTION 59. There is hereby created an auditing committee, which shall consist
of the mayor, president of the city council, and city auditor. The president of
the council shall be chairman of the committee and the city auditor secretary,
but in the absence of either from the meetings of the committee, a temporary
chairman or secretary may be chosen by the committee to act.
SECTION 59(1). It shall be the duty of the auditing committee to examine, and
allow or disallow, all claims and demands upon the city which may be presented,
except salaries of city officers as fixed by law or ordinance. The city auditor
shall not draw a warrant for any claim or demand against the city, except for
salaries aforesaid, unless the same has been approved by a majority of the
whole auditing committee.
SECTION 59(2). A claim or demand which is subject to the consideration of the
auditing committee shall be in writing, signed and certified by the claimant,
or some person authorized by him therefor, to be just, correct, legally due and
unpaid and must include or be accompanied by a detailed statement of the items
of charges and credits constituting it, as a part thereof. They shall be
presented to the auditor who shall file and number them in the order of
presentation, and refer them to the auditing committee at its next meeting. The
auditing committee may allow or reject a claim or demand in whole or in part.
The committee shall endorse upon the back thereof the date and amount of
allowance or partial allowance, and the particular fund from which payment is
to be made, or the date and fact of rejection. The endorsement shall be
verified by the signatures of the chairman and secretary of the auditing
committee.
   Ch. 226 S.L. 1947.
CLAIMS FOR DAMAGES
SECTION 59-A. All claims for damages against Boise City must be filed with the
city clerk within sixty (60) days after the time such damage shall have
occurred, specifying the time, place, character and cause of said damage, which
said claim shall be transmitted by the clerk to the council for its
consideration at the next regular meeting thereof. Unless claim has been filed
as hereinbefore provided within sixty days after the time such damage shall
have occurred, the council shall not authorize the payment of any such claim
and no action shall be maintained against said city for or on account of any
claim for such damages. If claim is filed within the time herein prescribed,
the council shall have sixty days after the filing of any such claim in which
to approve or reject the same, during which time no action shall be maintained
against Boise City.
   Ch. 31 S.L. 1941.
SINKING FUND COMMISSION-DUTIES
SECTION 60. 1. The mayor, auditor, treasurer and president of the council shall
constitute and be denominated a Sinking Fund Commission.
2.   Any three of the officers named in the last subdivision shall be and are
hereby authorized to discharge the trusts and duties hereby vested in them, but
shall not receive any additional salary or compensation for such services. The
council may require bonds from these officers for the faithful performance of
their duties as members of said commission.
3.   The Sinking Fund Commission shall negotiate the sale of all bonds of the
city, in accordance with the provisions of the ordinance under which such
bonds, may issue. They shall from time to time invest the money of the city set
apart for a sinking fund for the redemption of the city's bonded indebtedness,
in the purchase of bonds issued by the city at the market price, not exceeding
the par value thereof. If at any time such investment cannot be made, then said
commission may invest said funds in interest bearing securities of the county
of Ada, or the state of Idaho, or of the United States. No money belonging to
the sinking fund shall be loaned to any person or corporation.
4.   Whenever any of the moneys constituting the sinking fund shall be required
for investment, as above specified, or for the redemption of any city bonds at
their maturity, said commission shall report the amount of money so required to
the auditor, who shall certify such sum to the city council, and thereupon the
council shall authorize an order to be drawn on the treasurer, directing him
upon delivery of the securities purchased to pay for the same, or to make the
required payment of principal or interest maturing on the said bonds.
5.   It shall be the duty of the auditor to keep a correct journal of the
proceedings of said commission, to be verified by any three of them, and to
render to the city council once every three months, or oftener if required, a
full report of the proceedings of the commission. All acts of the commission
shall be based on resolutions, duly entered in said journal.
6.   In case of vacancy in office, or inability of any of said commissioners to
attend to the duties hereby imposed, it shall be the duty of the council to
designate by resolution one or more of their number to fill the place of such
commissioner or commissioners for the time being.
7.   It shall be the duty of said commissioners to protect the credit of the
city, direct and superintend the payment of interest and the bonded
indebtedness of the city, whenever said interest or bonds may be payable. All
bonds and securities purchased by said commission shall be held for safe
keeping by the treasurer. City bonds which have matured, been paid, and
returned to the treasurer, shall be destroyed in the presence of the
commission.
   S.L. 1907, pp. 90-91.
FRANCHISES
SECTION 61. (1) The rights of the city in and to its streets, avenues, parks,
bridges, and all other public places are hereby declared to be inalienable,
except as hereinafter otherwise provided.
(2)   No person, firm or corporation shall ever exercise any franchise or
privilege mentioned herein except in so far as he or it may be entitled to do
so by direct authority of the constitution of Idaho or the constitution or laws
of the United States, in, upon, over, under and along any street, alley,
highway or other public place in such city, unless he or it shall have obtained
a grant therefor in accordance with the provisions hereof.
(3)   Every franchise or privilege to construct or operate street, suburban or
interurban railroads along, upon, over or under any street, highway, or other
public place, or to lay pipes or conduits or to erect poles or wires or other
structures in, upon, over, under or along any street, alley, highway or other
public places in the city for the transmission of gas or electricity, or for
any purpose whatever, shall be granted upon the conditions herein provided, and
where not provided herein then as provided by general law.
(4)   An applicant for a franchisee or privilege shall file with the council an
application therefor, and thereupon the council shall, if it propose to grant
the same, advertise the fact of said application, together with a statement
that it is proposed to grant the same, in the official newspaper of the city.
The publication of such advertisement must be made in at least one issue of the
official newspaper before any further action can be taken on such application.
(5)   The advertisement must state the character of the franchise or privilege
it is proposed to grant, and, if it be a street, suburban or interurban
